lhs: Dot the two input transposes using their common batch list D, and left-last/right-penultimate contraction.
rhs: Dot the raw inputs in identity batch order, exchanging them exactly when P flips the last two slots, then apply the output transpose with batch mapping P of D and the same terminal orientation.
conditions: Legal common input transpose with batch prefix P; common original batch list D need not be sorted. One free and one contracted axis on each operand as derived from lawful equal-rank descriptors and source guards. Compatible paired extents and arbitrary static extents including zero.
types: Exact Int dense dot; arbitrary batch rank with one free axis per operand and one paired contracted axis.
overlap: The swap branch is definitionally the established operand-commutation/batch permutation result after normalization. Keep normalizes by reflexivity. One named input-transpose-removal optimization with two variants under the adopted expression-based gate, zero newly discovered algebraic identities.

lhs: Concatenate converted operands along a shared logical axis, then bitcast-convert back to the original word type.
rhs: Concatenate the original operands in their original order along that axis.
conditions: Nonempty ordered operand list; arbitrary shared static prefix/suffix shapes and per-operand concat-axis extents; equal bit widths or integral ratio k > 1. Rank-changing conversions use the final lane axis, disjoint from concat. One consistent least-first or most-first order. Covers zero extents.
types: Positive-width raw BitVec words or a complete trailing axis of k narrow words; arbitrary payload including sign bits. Exact logical bit observation; no physical-layout or implementation-level claim.
overlap: BitPackingProof.repack_compose/repack_refl and BitPackingShapeProof split/join are inherited inverse results without intervening concatenation. Ordered many-operand concatenation and all three width directions are one mathematical case; the caller delegates directly.

rhs: Remove the filter pad, set kernel size and dilation per modified spatial axis, then convolve.
conditions: Arbitrary spatial rank, zero feature/edge padding on filter, original dilation one where holes are added; legal positive stride and base/kernel dilation, signed window edges, reversal; compare shape and every value on each output-channel plane.
types: Exact Int; arbitrary feature count and static extents including zero.
overlap: Reuses PadDot sparse support. Output span, reversed and unreversed physical tap offsets and complete convolution sampling are additional obligations. Same transformation as exceptional filter case under a different arithmetic contract.

lhs: Convolve an explicitly edge-padded input with the kernel.
rhs: Move the edge amounts into the window and skip out-of-range taps.
conditions: One spatial axis, one input and output feature, unit stride and dilation, no reversal, arbitrary nonempty operand lists and nonnegative pad amounts.
types: Strict binary32 on a closed positive-zero, positive-infinity and NaN fragment. Observe NaN class.
overlap: Input edge versus skipped window position. The earlier semiring input-pad law excludes these multiplication rules.

lhs: Convolve with materialized zero taps between consecutive filter entries.
rhs: Convolve with the undilated stored filter and increase window dilation to jump over the holes.
conditions: One spatial axis, one input/output feature, unit stride and original dilation, no reversal or edges, nonempty arrays. All witness input positions are in bounds.
types: Strict binary32 on positive-zero, positive-infinity and NaN classes.
overlap: This is the exceptional arithmetic variant of filter-pad folding. The input-pad witness instead depends on skipping an out-of-bounds base position.

lhs: Evaluate the original costlier nested matrix product in its selected parenthesization.
rhs: Reassociate to the cheaper product and keep the original free-axis order.
conditions: Unbatched matrix products, strict modeled twofold cost threshold. Both orientations have a nonempty admitted witness. Inputs and intermediates lie in a finite nonnegative integer-valued RNE binary32 fragment. Only the direct output ordering is claimed.
types: Round-to-nearest-even on load, product and each sequential addition; pre-round integer ≤2^30.
overlap: The two cost orientations give a single reassociation law. Earlier semiring associativity and mixed-radix binary32 results do not establish it under fixed rounded accumulation.

lhs: Gather an indexed window from a padded operand with matching batch pad on the indices when present.
rhs: Gather from the unpadded operand and index rows, then pad the corresponding output batch and passthrough axes.
conditions: Static rank-three physical [batch,lookup,passthrough] operand, one explicit batching pair, full passthrough window and one clamped lookup component, arbitrary legal width, nonnegative result extents, signed edges/interior holes; passthrough-only uses identity batch and unchanged starts.
types: Arbitrary values and independent index fill, signed integer starts; every typed output and both edge paths.
overlap: Two source variants instantiate one pad transport, distinct from scalar Gather and the subsequent reshape-of-pad graph.

lhs: Narrow each wide array, concatenate on the newly appended lane dimension, and widen back.
rhs: Concatenate the original wide arrays along the same numbered dimension.
conditions: Static noncomplex words with divisible storage widths and ratio greater than one, equal original shapes. The original has an inferred result exactly for a unary concat on this axis; the replacement axis is outside the original rank. Earlier unary elimination can preempt this shape.
types: Shape preservation for logical arrays; e.g. U16[3] narrowed to U8[3,2].
overlap: Excluded new-lane domain of the shared-axis bit-identity proof. Count the shape refutation separately by declared domain; it supplies no native execution.
